en.html:
Her pilot was myself, and even I needed several seconds to understand the condition. Haan, partly because I had become upset...

But a tsurugi with whom she had no bond, and almost at once she understood what had happened? Small thing to say, not at all a small thing to do. Normally a smith only could manage that.

仕手の俺ですら、状態の把握に数秒は掛かった。

――些細な事のようで、中々に尋常な話ではない。
　普通、そんな真似ができるのは鍛冶師だけだろう。

en.html:
Kageaki"............"
Chachamaru"Sleep time."
Kageaki"To sleep, I agree."
Chachamaru"Yes."
Kageaki"..."
Chachamaru"Nya."
Kageaki"...Your Excellency. Your own room."
Chachamaru"Apun is staying here."
Kageaki"A little earlier, you expressly announced separate guest-room regulations."
Chachamaru"To the best of my very convenient memory, no such statement was made."
Kageaki"That is a politician's answer."
Chachamaru"Politician hi hoon, sir. My profession only."
Kageaki"...Indeed you are."
Chachamaru"Not the first time, either."
Kageaki"This morning?"
Chachamaru"Yes."
Kageaki"I thought you had judged when I would wake and come to attend—"
Chachamaru"No. Sleeping nearby every night since apun brought you here."
Kageaki"Procedurally, that is not satisfactory."
Chachamaru"You like having company, though."
Kageaki"Yes."
Chachamaru"Ah. Like it?"
Kageaki"Being human, I find congenial company agreeable. That does not settle the procedural question."
Chachamaru"Honest fellow. Full marks."
Kageaki"Your Excellency. A difficulty arises."
Chachamaru"I can sleep."
Kageaki"Pardon?"
Chachamaru"When you are here, na. Thoda sa... a little only."
Chachamaru"Pata nahi kyun. The other sounds go far away. Only your sound reaches me."
Chachamaru"Your sound does not torment apun..."

en.html:
Inside, whatever she was; outside, however she behaved—Chachamaru Ashikaga was still a girl making a plea.

To hear it and deliberately say no—

That much strength of will, apparently, was not available in me.

Chachamaru"Bhai."
Kageaki"Yes."
Chachamaru"Sleepy?"
Kageaki"Some fatigue remains in my body, so to an extent. Not enough to feel a weight on my eyelids."
Chachamaru"Right. Then one request."
Kageaki"What would that be?"
Chachamaru"Anything will do. Tell apun a story?"
Kageaki"...A story? But would that not interfere with your sleep?"
Chachamaru"Apun ka ulta hai. For me it is the opposite. Somebody talking nearby, and the noise stops demanding so much attention."
Chachamaru"If the voice itself is unpleasant, useless, obviously. Yours is all right."
Kageaki"............Understood. If that much will serve."
Chachamaru"Grateful."
Kageaki"...Then... Something that happened in the mountain-climbing club I belonged to as a student————"

ja.html:
茶々丸「お兄さん」
景明「はい」
茶々丸「眠い？」
景明「まだ身体に疲労が残っているようなので、 それなりには。 　目蓋に重さを感じる程ではありません」
茶々丸「そか。 　じゃ、一つお願い」
景明「どのような」
茶々丸「何でもいいから、お話してくれると嬉しい な」
景明「……話、ですか。 　しかし、眠る妨げになるのでは」
茶々丸「んー、あては逆なの。 　耳元で話し掛けられてると、雑音があまり 気にならなくなるから」
茶々丸「その声自体が不愉快だったら意味ないけど ね。 　お兄さんは、大丈夫」
景明「…………。 　わかりました。その程度の事なら」
茶々丸「感謝」
景明「……では…… 　学生時代、自分が所属していた山岳部での 出来事を――――」
